A fruit that shares a name with a color is orange.

Postmodernism is a broad movement that developed in the mid- to late-20th century across diverse fields, including literature. In relation to literature, it is characterized by a self-consciousness about the conventions of fiction, a rejection of the modernist rejection of tradition, and a tendency toward self-reference, irony, parody, and pastiche. Postmodern literature often questions the nature of reality, truth, and identity, frequently employing non-linear narratives, fragmented structures, and metafictional elements to challenge the reader's expectations and the idea of a single, objective truth.
